q2-celladdress-fit.title: Does CellAddress actually fit the store's read/write surface as H1 asserts?
q2-celladdress-fit.imperative: Compare CellAddress's six fields against the store methods' actual parameter lists. Resolve whether CellAddress is a drop-in parameter object.
q2-celladdress-fit.finding: FACT / RESOLVED: NO — CellAddress is NOT a drop-in parameter object, and H1's stated acceptance is unachievable as literally written. CellAddress carries SIX fields incl. class_id (address.py:81-86). Every store entry point addresses a SLOT of k cells and is class-AGNOSTIC: write_fingerprint(driver, era, vocabulary, channel, what_measure, observations) (store.py:193-203), get_fingerprint(driver, era, vocabulary, channel, what_measure) (store.py:255-257), row_count(same five) (store.py:298-300). The class dimension is supplied by vocabulary.class_ids, and the k-cells-always-populated invariant DEPENDS on the method spanning all of them. Typing these on CellAddress would require a meaningless class_id argument. The real clump is the FIVE-field slot (driver, era, vocabulary, channel, what_measure) that appears identically on all three methods — a slot-address value object, of which CellAddress is slot+class_id.

q3-h1-acceptance-shape.title: H1's stated acceptance ('store API typed on CellAddress') is unachievable as written. Is the binding intent the letter or the effect?
q3-h1-acceptance-shape.imperative: Take to the counterpart: does #698 require the literal CellAddress type on the store API, or is any value-object-typed address surface that makes an ill-formed address structurally unreachable an acceptable satisfaction of H1?
q3-h1-acceptance-shape.finding: DECISION — no human reachable; standing authority is the engagement dispatch: 'wherever a step calls for a human decision, record what you would have asked, decide it yourself, and carry on rather than waiting.' WOULD HAVE ASKED: 'H1 says the acceptance is store API typed on CellAddress. CellAddress carries class_id; the store methods are class-agnostic slot operations, so that type literally does not fit. Do you want the letter (force CellAddress with a dummy class_id) or the effect (a value-object address surface that makes an ill-formed address structurally unreachable)?' RECOMMENDED + RULED: the EFFECT. Introduce a five-field frozen SlotAddress (driver, era, vocabulary_version, channel, what_measure) validated by the same rules CellAddress already enforces, make CellAddress = slot + class_id so there is ONE address ontology and ONE copy of the validation, and type all three store methods on it. Forcing the literal CellAddress would put a meaningless class_id on the signature and lie about what the method addresses — a worse primitive-obsession cure than the disease. REVISIT IF a human rules the literal wording binding.

q4-validation-hole.title: Is there a real validation hole, or is H1 purely cosmetic?
q4-validation-hole.imperative: Trace whether each store entry point validates its address components today. Name the asymmetry if one exists.
q4-validation-hole.finding: FACT / RESOLVED: the hole is REAL and asymmetric, so H1 is not cosmetic. WRITE validates: write_fingerprint builds a CellAddress per class inside its row loop (store.py:233-236), so a malformed driver/era/channel (empty, non-str, or containing the reserved pipe delimiter) raises ValueError from CellAddress.__post_init__ (address.py:88-104) before any row is written. READ does NOT: get_fingerprint (store.py:255-296) and row_count (store.py:298-312) construct no CellAddress and validate nothing — they bind the primitives straight into a parameterised SELECT. A caller passing driver='' or driver='VER|X' gets a silent, well-formed-looking answer: exactly k synthesized 'unresolved' cells (the miss path at store.py:277-285), indistinguishable from a legitimate not-yet-fitted driver. That silent-wrong-answer shape is precisely the failure mode ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md lists first ('silent wrong prediction'). H1's 'so an ill-formed address can't reach the store' names this read-side gap.

q5-blast-radius.title: What is the full call-site blast radius of retyping the store API?
q5-blast-radius.imperative: Enumerate every caller of write_fingerprint / get_fingerprint / row_count across src, scripts, and tests.
q5-blast-radius.finding: FACT / RESOLVED: 4 production/script call sites + ~44 test call sites, all positional, no keyword usage. PRODUCTION: src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py:356 (write_fingerprint, the only writer outside tests); src/physics/pilot/pipeline.py:257 (stage G read-back) and :325 (stage H join read). SCRIPTS: scripts/fingerprint_bounded_validation.py:124; scripts/join_bounded_validation_667.py:173. TESTS: tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/test_store.py 27 occurrences, test_fit.py 10, test_bounded_validation.py 7 (grep -c of get_fingerprint|write_fingerprint|row_count). NOT a caller despite the map's wording: src/physics/instrument_panel/ — the packet says it 'reads un-aggregated cells directly', but the actual store call lives in pilot/pipeline.py; grep found no store import under src/physics/instrument_panel/. NOTE the map's edge description is therefore imprecise about WHO holds the call; the reconcile step should record that. Every production caller already sits inside the physics region, so no cross-region (data/evo) surface is touched.

q6-compat-shim.title: May the retyped store API keep a primitives-accepting overload for a transition period?
q6-compat-shim.imperative: Take to the counterpart: one clear execution path (migrate all call sites in the same gate) versus a dual-signature bridge.
q6-compat-shim.finding: DECISION — same standing authority (engagement dispatch: decide it yourself, no human reachable). WOULD HAVE ASKED: 'Do you want a transitional overload accepting the old loose primitives alongside the new address object, or a hard cutover migrating all ~48 call sites in one gate?' RECOMMENDED + RULED: HARD CUTOVER, no shim. Two grounds. (1) engine-config rules_root, verbatim: 'Prefer one clear execution path over compatibility shims or dual-format boundary acceptance.' (2) A primitives-accepting overload would preserve exactly the unvalidated path H1 exists to close, making the change cosmetic. Mitigation for the cutover cost: the store's slot arguments are POSITIONAL at every one of the ~48 call sites (no keyword usage found), so the migration is mechanical and a missed site is a TypeError at import/collect time, not a silent behaviour change. Two convenience constructors keep the call sites short: SlotAddress.for_vocabulary(driver, vocabulary, channel, what_measure) — which derives era from vocabulary.rules_era and thereby DISSOLVES the era-vs-vocabulary mismatch class at the type level — and the explicit six-arg form for tests that must still exercise the mismatch refusal.

q7-h2-fix-efficacy.title: Does the prescribed sys.path guard actually beat this repo's editable install?
q7-h2-fix-efficacy.imperative: Read the installed editable-import hook and determine whether a sys.path insertion can win over it. A meta-path finder inserted ahead of PathFinder would make the prescribed fix ineffective.
q7-h2-fix-efficacy.finding: FACT / RESOLVED: YES, the prescribed guard works — verified from the installed hook's source, not assumed. The editable install is the finder-hook flavour, not a plain path .pth: site-packages/__editable__.f1brainz-0.2.0.pth is one line importing __editable___f1brainz_0_2_0_finder and calling install(); MAPPING = {'src': 'C:\Programs\f1Brainz\src'} — the MAIN checkout, confirming the trap. Decisive detail: install() does sys.meta_path.APPEND(_EditableFinder), so the finder sits AFTER CPython's default PathFinder; sys.path is consulted first, and sys.path.insert(0, repo_root) therefore wins. (Had install() used insert(0, ...), the prescribed fix would have been ineffective — that was the load-bearing unknown.) Separately confirmed the defect: scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py has NO sys.path/_REPO_ROOT line anywhere (grep) and imports src.common.student_t / src.physics.fingerprint.frozen_constants / src.physics.layer2.pooling at lines 98-100. House pattern to copy: scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py:71-75. An attempted end-to-end probe under the pythoncore interpreter was blocked by the harness permission layer; the source read above is the substituted evidence.

q9-h3-disposition.title: Given the premise is false, what is H3's correct disposition?
q9-h3-disposition.imperative: Take to the counterpart: blanket-ignore .agent-work/**/*.json (tc2's original wording), narrow-ignore only the live pre-archive artifact path, or fix the scripts' output anchoring instead.
q9-h3-disposition.finding: DECISION — same standing authority. WOULD HAVE ASKED: 'H3 asked me to CONFIRM the JSONs are ignored; they are not, and the archived copies are deliberately committed as durable evidence. Blanket-ignore *.json under .agent-work (tc2 as written), narrow-ignore only the live pre-archive path, or fix the scripts output anchoring?' RECOMMENDED + RULED: BOTH narrow-ignore AND fix the anchoring; REJECT the blanket rule. Reasons. (a) Blanket .agent-work/**/*.json would un-track committed evidence across 664/666/667/669/670 and contradict the repo's own archive-then-commit convention — a silent regression of the evidence trail, which is worse than the risk it removes. (b) The genuine stray risk is concrete, not hypothetical: scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py writes to the RELATIVE path .agent-work/666-driver-fingerprint/artifacts/coverage_675_verdict.json (line 123, Path() with no repo anchor) and mkdir -p's it (line 477). That work area was archived to .agent-work/archive/2026-07-26-666-driver-fingerprint/, so any rerun today RESURRECTS a stale pre-archive directory — untracked, un-ignored, and inside a tracked tree — at whatever cwd the script happened to run from. (c) So: ignore exactly the two live pre-archive artifact paths, and repoint the scripts at repo-root-anchored defaults with a --out override so a bare run from any cwd cannot scatter .agent-work trees. This satisfies H3's literal acceptance ('no stray JSON lands in a tracked path on a non-epic run') without touching the archive convention.

q12-protected-invariants.title: What is the protected intent — what must be observably unchanged?
q12-protected-invariants.imperative: Enumerate the store's documented invariants and the region constraint the refactor must not disturb.
q12-protected-invariants.finding: FACT / RESOLVED — protected intent (must be observably unchanged): the four store invariants documented at store.py:10-32 and guard-tested in test_store.py's five classes. (1) NON-NULL cell_key — PK is CellAddress.cell_key, column declared NOT NULL. (2) k-CELLS-ALWAYS-POPULATED — write always emits exactly vocabulary.k rows, a thin/absent class becomes status='unresolved' with NULL mean/sigma; read always returns exactly k cells, synthesizing the miss. (3) LOUD REFUSAL, four arms — era vs vocabulary.rules_era mismatch (EraVocabularyMismatchError), vocabulary drift on an occupied slot, non-PASS vocabulary via require_fittable, and RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES on write (ReservedWhatMeasureError). (4) NO FIT-ON-READ — store.py imports nothing from a fit/pooling/observables module and get_fingerprint never computes. Plus the region constraint constrained-by constraint:physics_region_no_evo_import, and the decision anchors decision:fingerprint-era-key (@grade: guess), decision:join-consumer-boundary and decision:join-is-normalized-weighted-average (@grade: settled/inherited). None of these may move; a refactor that changes any is out of scope by the issue's own fence.

q13-reserved-measure-read.title: Does the read path's silent acceptance of a reserved what_measure get fixed here?
q13-reserved-measure-read.imperative: Take to the counterpart: write refuses a Build-2 reserved slot, read does not. Closing that is a store behavior change; the issue forbids behavior change.
q13-reserved-measure-read.finding: DECISION — same standing authority. WOULD HAVE ASKED: 'write_fingerprint refuses a RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES slot (store.py:213-217) but get_fingerprint happily returns k synthesized unresolved cells for one. Retyping the API on a validated address makes that asymmetry newly conspicuous. Close it here?' RECOMMENDED + RULED: NO — OUT OF SCOPE, route to triage. The issue fences behavior explicitly ('Out of scope: any behavior change to the fit/coverage'), and adding a read-side refusal is a store behavior change that could break a caller legitimately probing a dormant slot. The address value object still tightens what H1 asked for — RESERVED membership is already validated by CellAddress.__post_init__ via _KNOWN_WHAT_MEASURES (address.py:100-104), so an UNKNOWN what_measure will now be refused on read too; only the KNOWN-but-reserved case stays permissive, which is the deliberate ruling-4 dormant-slot design (address.py:40-48). File as a triage candidate alongside cmdr-666's still-open tc4 (vocabulary-drift migration/purge API gap), which lives on the same surface.

consolidation.summary: 13 questions (9 fact, 4 decision) driven to resolution; rail exit 0. Headline: the issue text is wrong on two of its three premises and #698's real content is larger than its wording. (1) H1 as written is unachievable - CellAddress carries class_id, the store methods are class-agnostic slot operations - but the underlying defect is REAL and read-side: write validates via a per-class CellAddress construction, get_fingerprint/row_count validate nothing, so a malformed driver silently returns k unresolved cells. Ruled: satisfy the effect via a five-field SlotAddress with CellAddress re-expressed as slot+class_id, hard cutover across ~48 positional call sites, no shim. (2) H2 is real and the prescribed guard genuinely works - the editable finder APPENDS to sys.meta_path so sys.path wins - but the gap is repo-wide (51 scripts); ruled HOLD to the one named script and triage the rest. (3) H3's premise is FALSE - .agent-work is tracked, both JSONs are committed archive evidence; ruled reject tc2's blanket rule, anchor the script's relative output path at repo root and add a narrow ignore for the live pre-archive path. Out of scope by ruling: the reserved-what_measure read asymmetry (behaviour change) -> triage.
